inputs: All 14 existing frozen cases, exact text, tags, type, query, direction, label, source-channel filter and topK. No generated answer.

encoder.vocabulary: sorted union of tokens in all fixture source bodies and queries, excluding tags, labels, keys and oracle

arms.nativeTopK: Unmodified store.search on source namespace, query, exact sourceChannel/type filter and original topK. Record zero scores without filtering.
arms.nativeWide: Same native search with limit topK+8. This changes retrieval budget and is a separate wider-search control.
arms.applicationOneHop: Benchmark application: native topK search; keep positive-score seeds only; search edge namespace by exact fromId, bounded 64+1 total edges and up to8 seeds; get outgoing targets once; honor original source/type filters; deduplicate and append up to8 distinct targets, no recursive/reverse traversal. Do not require neighbor query similarity; labels are stored without interpretation. No conflict, trust, token or receipt policy is invented for the SDK.

resourceBoundary.network: OS sandbox denies all network; fresh in-process store per case
resourceBoundary.identity: namespaces are application-provided; no authentication/ACL model tested
resourceBoundary.tokenBudget: same requested Lite budget retained as context; native SDK does not accept it. Record returned UTF8 body bytes without calling them model tokens. No relative latency ranking vs Lite HTTP/H2.

lifecycle.method: fresh store per mutation; actual put/delete; read native exact source and edge; rerun native search/application one-hop; compare detached client snapshot with live get object
lifecycle.receipt: not exercised on SDK; null is not evidence of a product-wide absence

checks: native scores equal independent term-frequency cosine calculation
native rank limits and original metadata filter apply
application results independently reconstructible from native seeds/edges/gets
query-free link can be followed by application
source correction/delete and edge-delete reflected in current APIs
held client snapshots are not server freshness claims
interpretation: Matched input and observed evidence availability only. Different rankers and native contracts; application adapter is not an upstream graph feature. No answer-quality, policy win-rate, persistence, access-control, cost or competitor-wide superiority claim.
